text.p: Caledonian Pacific Minerals NL said on Monday it had received encouraging results from test drilling at its Nundle gold prospect in New South Wales.

The results included gradings of two to five metres at 5.86 grams of gold a tonne (g/t) and 38 metres at 0.35 g/t and indicate the prospectivity for thick vein moderate grade intersections, the company said.
At 11:43 a.m (0043 GMT), Caledonian shares were unchanged at 23 Australian cents.
Most of the intersections were related to shear zones and quartz vein systems and lodes which old mines lie on, the company said.
However, there was widespread alteration zoning with associated low-grade mineralisation surrounding many of the interesections, Caledonian said.
These alteration systems may reflect alteration zoning associated with potential porphyry-style intrusive systems, the company said. More test drilling is planned, it said.
